meta.title: 04.11.2026 Democratii castiga alegerile iar AMD raporteaza stelar!!!
meta.thread_line: 6 threads · AMD's record quarter · SpaceX back above $140 · Oracle's $20B financing · thin-breadth rebound and yields · midterms and portfolio sensitivity · GYW portfolio moves

snapshot: Source note: built from GrowYourWealth's pasted written daily note (no captions or video link), so figures are as the author states them.
Stance: look through any short-term event and keep buying stocks; he expects the election result to let the "AI bubble" stabilize, things to calm from Monday and a good year-end.
**AMD** Q3: revenue $13.377B (+45%), Data Center $8.5B (+97%, now ~64% of revenue), Q4 guide $17B ±3% (~+27% q/q); Client and Gaming fell 8% to $3.7B, so growth rests on one engine.
Nov 3 close was a **thin rebound**: Nasdaq +0.83% but most S&P 500 stocks fell, the Dow lost 0.38%, and US10Y rose toward 4.95% after 7.5M job openings.

**Oracle** +5.89% to $126.25 after -8.76% on Monday; the $20B raise (86.2M shares at $116 plus $10B bonds at 7.00-8.65%) brings dilution and heavier debt, so the test is OCI revenue, capex and free cash flow.
**SpaceX** (SPCX) closed $141.31, back above $140, but he says the correction is not over and position weight matters.
Midterms: Democrats projected to win the House with surprise Senate gains, not yet certified; he sees no reason to liquidate strategic positions, only to hold cash and scale in.
Catalysts: ADP at 15:15 Romania time on Nov 4, Oracle financing close Nov 4, NFP on Nov 6 at 15:30.

themes.title: AMD's record Q3 and $17B guide confirm AI demand, with one engine carrying the growth
themes.lead: He calls the print fundamentally positive, but wants regular-session volume, not the 23:00 enthusiasm, to confirm it.
bullets: Revenue **$13.377B** (+45% y/y); Data Center $8.5B (+97%); GAAP net income $2.428B (+95%), GAAP EPS $1.46 (+95%), adjusted EPS $2.09 (+74%); adjusted gross margin 56%, up 2 points.
Q4 guide $17B ±3%, about +66% y/y at the midpoint and roughly +27% quarter over quarter; he reads it as AI infrastructure spending turning into paid, delivered orders.
Data Center is now ~64% of revenue; management expects faster growth in Q4 as production of the Helios platforms and Venice processors expands.
The weaker part: Client and Gaming revenue fell 8% y/y to $3.7B, so a business leaning on one engine needs it to run flawlessly every quarter.
Tuesday regular close $483.90 (+3.65%); after-hours indication near $508 (~5% higher), which he says often evaporates in the first 30 minutes of the next session.
Levels: support $473-480 (Tuesday's range); resistance $497-500, then $508-513.

themes.title: SpaceX is back above $140, but the correction isn't over and the AI spend is unproven
themes.lead: He calls SpaceX a strategic priority yet warns that AMD's results do not prove SpaceX's own AI projects will earn satisfactory returns.
bullets: Tuesday close **$141.31** (+3.62%), low $137.50, high $142.74, volume over 73 million shares; Monday closed $136.37 after the late-October correction.
Instrument check: in his data SPCX is the stock of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. on Nasdaq, not a fund or leveraged product; he tells readers to verify the instrument before any order.

Three economic engines: launches, satellite connectivity and AI infrastructure investment. Starlink is recurring communications revenue the market pays high multiples for; launch benefits from rocket reuse competitors still struggle to match.

His view of the main advantage is the integration of launch infrastructure with satellite services; the activities need enormous investment and the valuation must ultimately be backed by profit and cash flow.
Levels: support $137-138, then $134-136; resistance $142.74-145, then $148-150. Holding $140 and clearing $143-145 would extend the rebound; losing $137-138 raises odds of a return to $134-136.

themes.title: Oracle rebounds, but the $20B financing puts dilution and 7-8.65% debt on the clock
themes.lead: Demand for Oracle's compute is real; the risk is timing between building data centers and collecting multi-year contract revenue.
bullets: Tuesday close **$126.25** (+5.89%) after -8.76% on Monday; volume over 82 million shares, range $121.35-128.10.

Announced Nov 2: 86,206,897 new shares at $116 (~$10B) plus $10B of bonds with coupons between 7.00% and 8.65%; expected close Nov 4; proceeds may fund investment, debt repayment and general purposes.
Management targets over **$225B** annual revenue by fiscal 2030, which he says needs exceptional, not just good, operational execution.
Risks: share issue dilutes, bond coupons raise obligations, free cash flow stays under pressure while the company builds before it collects.
Three indicators he tracks: OCI revenue growth, capital spending, and when free cash flow turns positive.
Levels: support $121-122, then $118-119 and the $116 issue price (a financial marker, not a guaranteed support); resistance $128-131.

themes.title: A tech-led rebound on thin participation, with yields rising again
themes.lead: The index was held up by a few large caps, so he calls it constructive but not a healthy recovery of the whole market.
bullets: Most S&P 500 stocks closed red; Nvidia rose ~2.3%, Microsoft and Amazon helped, Apple fell ~1.9% on component-cost and margin worries.
He wants broader participation, a steadier VIX (about 20.8, slightly lower) and Russell 2000 resilience before calling it a recovery.
US10Y ~4.95% and US2Y ~4.61%, both higher, after ~7.5 million September job openings; higher rates hit first the companies funding expansion with borrowed money.
WTI about $96, still falling on Iran de-escalation talk; he builds no thesis on negotiations.

For Nov 4: positive case (AMD holds gains, Oracle stabilizes, yields calm) has the Nasdaq testing 25,500-25,600; base case is consolidation with rotation between AI and other sectors; negative case (yields up, election uncertainty, AMD sold at the open) makes 25,200-25,000 important. Levels are references, not predictions.

themes.status: DEMOCRATS PROJECTED TO WIN HOUSE · NOT CERTIFIED
themes.title: Democrats gain at the midterms; he maps how each holding is exposed, and does not liquidate
themes.lead: Political repricing is a 1-4 week volatility risk and a 3-12 month policy question, and he says it doesn't change Fed policy or the competitive position of his holdings.
bullets: Per Associated Press and Reuters, Democrats won Senate races in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio and made governor gains; control of both chambers is not final and results are projections, not legal certification.
First market reaction: US index futures down, Asian AI stocks under pressure, dollar weaker, Treasuries up (yields down), which prices a less friendly Congress and more tech regulation.
Next 1-4 weeks (mechanisms, not a forecast): higher index volatility, selective pressure on AI names, possibly lower US10Y, weaker dollar, higher VIX.
Main near-term risk is a further correction in high-valuation growth if stricter AI rules are priced; lower yields are the offset.

3-12 months: scenario A (Democrat House, Republican Senate) is a divided Congress with less risk of fast fiscal change but budget fights; scenario B (both chambers) means stronger oversight, investigations and budget leverage, tempered by the presidential veto and Senate procedure.

Sensitivity: high for ORCL, NBIS, IREN (AI rules, financing), PLTR and ONDS (defense and federal budgets), META (AI, privacy, antitrust); medium-high for SPCX, RKLB, ASTS, AMD, AVGO, TSLA, SOFI, HOOD; medium for LEU.

Three priorities: keep a cash reserve, monitor combined weight of AI and financing-dependent names, and scale in only where fundamentals justify the valuation; he would not liquidate strategic positions, nor use every dip for aggressive buying.

themes.title: GYW portfolio after Tuesday: Nebius and IREN snap back, and why not to oversize them
themes.lead: Apart from AMD, he jokes the rest of the portfolio was carnage, yet most names closed green, with the high-volatility ones moving most.
bullets: Nebius **$151.64** (+7.25%) after -8.27% the session before; support $143-145, resistance $152-155; GPU demand is the catalyst, financing and utilization decide profit.
IREN $24.46 (+11.08%, volume ~55M), the portfolio's best day; support $22-22.50, resistance $24.70-25; funding and energy-cost risks have not vanished.

Broadcom $332.13 (+3.07%): exposed to custom accelerators and networking; support $326-327, resistance $335-336. META $621.03 (+2.36%): watch capex versus free cash flow; support $610, resistance $625.

PLTR $175.40 (-1.65%): strong revenue growth but valuation and slower new contracts penalized; support $165-168, resistance $176-178. TSLA $398.50 (-1.32%): autonomy, energy, auto margins; support $396-397, resistance $406-407.
RKLB $54.43 (+4.53%): Neutron execution; ASTS $37.15 (+2.26%): launches, approvals, partnerships; SOFI $16.77 (+1.02%), HOOD $85.68 (+2.19%), ONDS $5.79 (+0.70%), LEU $95.67 (+0.81%).
Conclusion: a concentrated growth portfolio can gain from AI yet be hit at once by valuation compression, rising rates or tighter funding; sizing, cash reserve and staged buying matter.

takeaways.title: Hold through short-term events; his 20-year habit is to keep buying stocks and expect a good year-end.
Judge a rebound by breadth, VIX and the Russell 2000, not the Nasdaq print alone; Tuesday's rise rested on a few large caps.
Wait for regular-session volume before trusting an after-hours AMD pop; extended-hours gains often vanish in 30 minutes.
Track OCI revenue, capex and the turn to positive free cash flow; count dilution and 7-8.65% debt before calling it cheap.
Keep cash, cap the combined weight of AI and financing-dependent names, and scale in only where fundamentals back the price.
Watch ADP on Nov 4 (15:15 Romania time) and NFP on Nov 6 (15:30), plus Oracle's financing close.
